## 1a: mean function without NA handling

```{r}
v = c(1:50, 55)
vector_mean <- function( df){
  tot = 0
  for ( element in df){
    tot = tot + element
  }
  return( tot / length(df))
}

vector_mean( v)

```

# 1b: mean with NA handled
```{r}
super_vector_mean <- function( vector , na.rm = F ){
  tot = 0
  for (element in vector){
    if( is.na(element)){
      if(na.rm){
        next
      }else{
        return( NA)
      }
    }
    tot = tot +element
  }
   n = sum( !is.na(vector))
  return( tot / n) 
}

super_vector_mean(v , na.rm = T)

mean( v , na.rm =F)

```
##### My loop base function for "mean" are expected to agree because I included lines that handle presence of NA values within passed vector during iteration. The final sample size is also calculated by first turning the  NAs into  logicals ( TRUE/FALSE) then summing , which adds all the TRUEs(1s) to produce actual sample size since the FALSEs will be 0s.

# 1c: accessing data from DuckDB repository

```{r}
library(repoquet)
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)
library(ggplot2)


config_path <- "repoquet_public_example/repository_config.R"
cfg <- load_repository_config( config_path)

  FormattedDBPath = cfg$FormattedDBPath,
  DBName = cfg$DBName,
  TempDirPath = temp_dir,

nhanes_tables <- sort(grep("^NHANES_" , nhanes_tables, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE))

DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste0("DESCRIBE ", nhanes_table))


bmi_data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste0( "SELECT * FROM ", DBI::dbQuoteIdentifier(con, nhanes_table)))

str(bmi_data)

#column to calculate mean from 
weight_in_kg <- bmi_data$BMXWT
super_vector_mean( weight_in_kg , na.rm = T)
#regular mean function
mean( weight_in_kg , na.rm = T)


```

## 1d:  Testing for correlation between the BMXBMI vs BMXWAIST

Ho: correlation between body mass index and waist circumference = 0
Ha: correlation between body mass index and waist circumference != 0


```{r}
body_mass_index <- bmi_data $BMXBMI
waist_circum <- bmi_data $ BMXWAIST

cor.test( body_mass_index , waist_circum)


```
From the cor.test results;
there's a positive correlation ( r =0.9311994 ) between body mass index and waist circumference.
As BMI increases, waist circumference also increases.
t = 827.9 and p-value < 2.2e-16 suggest there's evidence for the alternative hypothesis. This shows relationship does not imply causation, but rather suggest it's worth investigating further.

## 2a. Downloading  dataset from GEO using the GEODataDownload function.

```{r}

library(DESeq2)
library(limma)
library(data.table)
library(GEOquery)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(DT)

#------Function--

GEODataDownload <- function(DS, gpl, gsm, PlateAnnotInfo, GenerateMetaData, Technology){
  library(DESeq2); library(limma); library(data.table)
  if(Technology == "Array"){
    gset <- getGEO(DS)
    if(length(gset) > 1) idx <- grep(gpl, attr(gset, "names")) else idx <- 1
    gset <- gset[[idx]]
    fvarLabels(gset) <- make.names(fvarLabels(gset))
    comp <- gsub(" ", "", gsm)
    comp <- gsub(",", "", comp)
    gsms <- paste0(comp)
    #### Set up raw names ####
    sml <- c()
    for(i in 1:nchar(gsms)){ sml[i] <- substr(gsms,i,i)}
    ex <- exprs(gset)
    qx <- as.numeric(quantile(ex, c(0., 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.99, 1.0), na.rm=T))
    LogC <- (qx[5] > 100) ||
      (qx[6]-qx[1] > 50 && qx[2] > 0) ||
      (qx[2] > 0 && qx[2] < 1 && qx[4] < 2)
    if(LogC){ ex[which(ex <= 0)] <- NaN
    exprs(gset) <- log2(ex) }
    sml <- paste("G", sml, sep="")
    f1 <- as.factor(sml)
    gset$description2 <- f1
    design <- model.matrix(~description2 + 0, gset)
    colnames(design) <- levels(f1)
    fit <- lmFit(gset, design)
    cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(G1-G0, levels = design)
    fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
    fit2 <- eBayes(fit2, 0.01)
    tT <- topTable(fit2, adjust="fdr", sort.by = "B", number = 25000000000)
    #### subset ####
    ex2 <- data.table(subset(tT, select=c("ID", "logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")))
    ex2$ID <- as.character(ex2$ID)
    #### annotate with gene names ####
    plat <- PlateAnnotInfo[GPLID == gpl,][,!"GPLID", with = FALSE]
    if(nrow(plat) == 0){ print(paste("There is no annotation information available for", gpl)) }
    plat$ID <- as.character(plat$ID)
    plat <- plat[!duplicated(plat$ID),]
    ex2 <- merge(plat, ex2, by = "ID")
    ex2$ID <- as.character(ex2$ID)
    exraw <- data.table(ex)
    exraw$ID <- as.character(rownames(ex))
    #### annotate raw data with gene names ####
    ex2 <- merge(ex2, exraw, by = "ID")
    #### Generate Meta Data ####
    Pdat <- pData(gset)
    #### Add Meta data ####
    Pdat <- as.data.table(Pdat)
    return(list(Data = ex2, MetaData = Pdat))
  }
  
  if(Technology == "RNAseq"){
    ACC <- paste("acc=", DS, sep = "")
    file <- paste("file=", DS, "_raw_counts_GRCh38.p13_NCBI.tsv.gz", sep = "")
    comp <- gsub(" ", "", gsm)
    comp <- gsub(",", "", comp)
    gsms <- paste0(comp)
    #### Set up DEG names ####
    urld <- "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/download/?format=file&type=rnaseq_counts"
    path <- paste(urld, ACC, file, sep="&");
    tbl <- as.matrix(data.table::fread(path, header=T, colClasses="integer"), rownames="GeneID")
    exraw <- tbl 
    apath <- paste(urld, "type=rnaseq_counts", "file=Human.GRCh38.p13.annot.tsv.gz", sep="&")
    annot <- tryCatch(data.table::fread(apath, header=T, quote="", stringsAsFactors=F, data.table=F),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
    ## FALLBACK (only change to the notes' function): if NCBI serves a captcha page instead of the
    ## annotation file, use NCBI's Homo_sapiens.gene_info (the same GeneID/Symbol/description source)
    if(is.null(annot) || !all(c("GeneID", "Symbol", "Description") %in% names(annot))){
      annot <- data.table::fread("https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/DATA/GENE_INFO/Mammalia/Homo_sapiens.gene_info.gz",
                                 header=T, quote="", stringsAsFactors=F, data.table=F)
      names(annot)[names(annot) == "#tax_id"] <- "tax_id"
      annot <- annot[, c("GeneID", "Symbol", "description")]
      names(annot)[3] <- "Description"
    }
    rownames(annot) <- annot$GeneID
    sml <- strsplit(gsms, split="")[[1]]
    sel <- which(sml != "X")
    sml <- sml[sel]
    tbl <- tbl[ ,sel]
    gs <- factor(sml)
    groups <- make.names(c("Ctrl", "Tx"))
    levels(gs) <- groups
    sample_info <- data.frame(Group = gs, row.names = colnames(tbl))
    keep <- rowSums( tbl >= 10 ) >= min(table(gs))
    tbl <- tbl[keep, ]
    ds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData=tbl, colData=sample_info, design= ~Group)
    ds <- DESeq(ds, test="Wald", sfType="poscount")
    r <- results(ds, contrast=c("Group", groups[2], groups[1]), alpha=0.05, pAdjustMethod ="fdr")
    tT <- r[order(r$padj)[1:length(r$padj)],]
    tT <- merge(as.data.frame(tT), annot, by=0, sort=F)
    tT <- subset(tT, select=c("GeneID","padj","pvalue","lfcSE","stat","log2FoldChange","baseMean","Symbol","Description"))
    #### subset ####
    ex2 <- data.table(subset(tT, select=c("GeneID", "Symbol", "Description", "log2FoldChange", "pvalue", "padj")))
    #### Adjust column names ####
    setnames(ex2, c("GeneID", "Symbol", "Description"), c("ENTREZID", "SYMBOL", "GENENAME"))
    #### Get Raw data ####
    GeneID <- as.integer(rownames(exraw))
    exraw <- as.data.table(exraw)
    #### Update column names ####
    exraw$ENTREZID <- GeneID
    #### merge FC and raw data together ####
    mer <- merge(ex2, exraw, by = "ENTREZID")
    return(mer)
  }
}

```

## 2b: adding column to data frame


```{r}

gse226151_data $ Subset_Comparison <- "Sarcopenia-HealthyAged"

```
An additional column describing the treatment comparison, it becomes easier to filter when making multiple analysis especially on same genes across multiple contrast and becomes a unique character for "grouping by" when combining multiple differential expression analyses.

## 2f: volcano plot of the differential expression results (log2 fold change on the x-axis, −log10
 adjusted p-value on the y-axis) in ggplot2
 
 
```{r}

volc_df<- gse226151_data[!is.na(gse226151_data$padj) & !is.na(gse226151_data$log2FoldChange), ]

volc_df$negLogPadj <- -log10(volc_df$padj)


fin <- max(volc_df$negLogPadj[is.finite(volc_df$negLogPadj)])

volc_df$negLogPadj[is.infinite(volc_df$negLogPadj)] <- fin * 1.05

volc_df$Category <- ifelse(volc_df$padj < 0.05 & abs(volc_df$log2FoldChange) > 1,
                        "Significant & |log2FC| > 1",
                 ifelse(volc_df$padj < 0.05, "Significant (padj < 0.05)",
                 ifelse(abs(volc_df$log2FoldChange) > 1, "|log2FC| > 1 only",
                        "Not significant")))

ggplot(
  volc_df,  aes( log2FoldChange , negLogPadj , color = Category) )+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40")+
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40")+
    labs(title = "Volcano plot: pre-sarcopenia + sarcopenia vs healthy aged (GSE226151)",
       x = "log2 fold change (Sarcopena / HealthyAged)",
       y = "-log10(adjusted p-value)") 
  


```
Interpretation:  The various points make up all the genes present. the 2 comparison groups, sarcopena and healthyAged are separated at the origin; right and left respectively. the y-axis represents statistical confidence and genes above the the horizontal line are more significant with p<0.05.
Biologically, the colored corner points are the genes whose expression in skeletal muscle differs between the sarcopenia  and healthy aging strongly enough to influence or induce carcopenic muscles, but this does not conclude that all points indicating folding  or significance are biologically reliable.
 
 
## 2g: MA plot (average expression on the x-axis, log2 fold change on the y-axis) via ggplot2

```{r}
ma_df <- data.frame(
  mean_expression = row_avg_perGene,
  log2FoldChange =  gse226151_data$log2FoldChange,
   padj = gse226151_data$padj
)

ma_df$significant <- ifelse(ma_df$padj < 0.05,
                            "Significant (padj < 0.05)", "Not significant")

ggplot( ma_df , 
        aes( x = mean_expression , y = log2FoldChange , colour = significant ))+
  geom_point( size = 1, alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_hline( yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed")+
  labs(
    title =" MA plot of sarcopenia vs healthy aged",
    x = "mean gene expressions",
    y = "log2 fold change for Tx vs ctl"
  )+ theme_bw()

```

The above MA plot demonstrates how much each gene is expressed on average along the x-axis Vs how much much it regulation influence on treatment it has. genes above the origin (0) are up-regulated while those below are down-regulated in treatment.
While MA plot check for whether fold changes are consistent expression levels, Volcana plot put the significance on the y-axis to show which genes in particular are confidently changed.


## 3a. SummarizedExperiment with at minimum two assay matrices in gse226151_data

```{r}
library(SummarizedExperiment)

sampleCols <- grep("^GSM", colnames(gse226151_data), value = TRUE)

groups <- rep(c("0", "X", "1"), c(20, 19, 19))

names(groups) <- sampleCols
subb <- names(groups)[groups != "X"]


RowNames <- as.character(gse226151_data$ENTREZID) 
countMat <- as.matrix(gse226151_data[ , ..subb])

dimnames(countMat) <- list(RowNames, subb)
logCPMMat <- log2(t(t(countMat) / colSums(countMat)) * 1e6 + 1)
dimnames(logCPMMat) <- dimnames(countMat)


RowData <- data.frame(SYMBOL = gse226151_data$SYMBOL,
                      log2FoldChange = gse226151_data$log2FoldChange,
                      padj = gse226151_data$padj,
                      row.names = RowNames)

ColData <- data.frame(Treatment = ifelse(groups[subb] == "1", "Tx", "Ctrl"),
                      row.names = subb)

SE <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = countMat, logCPM = logCPMMat),
                           rowData = RowData, colData = ColData)
SE

```
## 3b: row and column names verification

```{r}
identical(rownames(ColData), colnames(countMat))
identical(rownames(ColData), colnames(logCPMMat))
identical(rownames(RowData), rownames(countMat))

(SE <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = countMat, logCPM = logCPMMat),
                            rowData = RowData, colData = ColData))
```
## 3c: subsetting the SummarizedExperiment
```{r}

#i : treatment samples using the column metadata

SE_treatment <- SE[, colData(SE)$Treatment == "Tx"]
dim(SE_treatment)


#ii: Selecting only significantly differentially expressed genes (adjusted p-value < 0.05) using the row metadata.

sig_expressed_genes <- SE[ !is.na (rowData(SE)$padj) & rowData(SE)$padj < 0.05, ]

# iii: Combining both filters simultaneously.

SE_Tx_Sig <- SE[!is.na(rowData(SE)$padj) & rowData(SE)$padj < 0.05, colData(SE)$Treatment == "Tx"]
```



## 3d: Access the raw expression values for the top 5 differentially expressed genes 

```{r}

top5_by_p.value <- rownames(SE)[order(rowData(SE)$padj)][1:5]
top5Counts <- assays(SE)[["counts"]][top5_by_p.value, ]
rownames(top5Counts) <- paste0(rowData(SE)[top5_by_p.value, "SYMBOL"], " (", top5_by_p.value, ")")

tbl <- data.frame( top5Counts)


```

## 3e:
SummarizedExperiment  holds the expression matrices, the gene annotations and the sample annotations in one object, and it keeps them aligned by name. Rows always matching gens and coulumns matching samples keeps the data in sync and ensure ease access.
rows always match genes, columns always match samples. SE would be preferred over dataframe when dealing with genomic data with many samples per gene with additional metadata.Also, with dealing with data that has 2 axes, SE will be better than dataframe.


## 4.
Bioconductor objects orient data with genes as rows and samples as columns because genomic data metadata such as gene IDs, symbols, coordinates, DE statistics compared to the columns which often carry gene names. analyses can also be applied to rows more broadly.
But stats tools like lm() expect the opposite thus one sample per row transposing.
